scenario: The ego vehicle attempts to overtake a slower lead vehicle on a two-lane rural highway when the lead vehicle simultaneously initiates its own overtaking maneuver, resulting in a near-miss side-swipe collision.

ego.behavior: The car travels forward and attempts to overtake the slower lead vehicle by moving into the opposing lane.

adversarials.behavior: The car travels forward and unexpectedly initiates an overtaking maneuver to pass slower traffic ahead, moving into the opposing lane at the same time as the ego vehicle.
The truck travels forward ahead of the other vehicles in the same lane, serving as the slower traffic that the lead car attempts to overtake.
The car travels forward ahead of the lead vehicle in the same lane, serving as additional slower traffic in the roadway.
The motorcycle travels forward in the opposing lane toward the ego and lead vehicle during their simultaneous overtaking maneuvers.

spatial_relation: The ego vehicle is on a two-lane rural highway with an uphill curve, positioned behind a lead car that is behind slower traffic including a truck and a white car; a motorcycle approaches in the opposing lane.
requirements_and_restrictions: Initial distances are defined between the ego vehicle and the lead vehicle ahead, and the scenario terminates after the near-miss or side-swipe collision event occurs.

road_side_structures.position: Positioned along the left side of the highway on the concrete barrier.

reasoning_chain: 1. Actors: Ego is the dashboard-camera vehicle; adversarials are the black lead car, red truck, white car, and oncoming motorcycle. 2. Enumeration: four adversarials identified. 3. Chronology: initially ego follows black car which follows truck/white car; midpoint black car and ego both swerve left into opposing lane simultaneously; ending near-miss occurs as black car cuts across ego. 4. Evidence: black car's leftward drift and ego's matching trajectory create overlap; motorcycle's approach in opposing lane confirms two-way traffic layout.
